Sort, order and solve picture clues

Use every clue to sort, order and decide.

  1. See it

This chapter works best after Coins, prices and change. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can find what does not belong.
  • I can find someone's place in a row.
  • I can follow a picture change or route.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 3

Use every clue

Read all the clues before you answer.

Each clue rules something out.

Screen 2 of 3

Find the odd one out

Look at what the things have in common.

Three can roll. One cannot. The one that cannot is the odd one out.

Screen 3 of 3

Where is it in the row?

First, second, third, fourth.

Count from the start of the row, not from your own place.

Words to know
clue
A small fact that helps you work out the answer.
odd one out
The one that is different from the others.
order
First, second, third. Where each one stands in a row.

For parents

What your child learns

Order puzzles need every clue. Thickest and thinnest are the two ends of a size line. In a pair, the first change tells you the rule to repeat on the second pair.

A common slip

Children may answer for only one part of the question, such as the thickest but not the thinnest. Underline each thing asked and answer both. Check the order with a line.

5-minute home activity: Thick and thin

  1. Find 4 books or pads of different thickness.
  2. Line them from thinnest to thickest.
  3. Say which is thickest and which is thinnest.
  4. Make a rule, like turn it round, and ask your child to repeat it.
